dateLabel: c. 2450-2140 BCE (earliest known in central Europe)
title: Milk-digesting gene (lactase persistence)
summary: Ancient DNA finds the earliest known European carrier of the adult milk-digestion variant between 2450 and 2140 BCE. It then spread fast in some herding peoples. When it first arose is debated.
why: Culture (dairying) changed human genes, not just the other way round.
interchange: East African herders evolved lactase persistence independently, with different mutations
